testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: A 40-foot-long item on a flatbed trailer needs at least ____ tie-down(s).
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo length. Always use at least two tie-downs, no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, what is the safest driving speed?

options.text: The same speed as surrounding traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other vehicles in heavy traffic. When two vehicles travel in the same direction at the same speed, they cannot hit each other.

questions.question: What endorsement test do you need to transport hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: You need a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any size vehicle that carries defined classes of hazardous materials.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing in a placarded vehicle, you should always:

options.text: Stop within five feet of the tracks.
Change gears while on the tracks.
Change lanes while on the tracks.

questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with a placarded vehicle, stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail. Turn on your four-way flashers while crossing. Do not stop, change gears, or change lanes while crossing the tracks.

questions.question: How often must drivers check that cargo is secure?
questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every 150 miles or every three hours after that.

questions.question: What brake system do most heavy-duty vehicles use?
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brake systems controlled by one set of controls.

questions.question: A lightly loaded cargo van is usually:

options.text: The same height as when carrying a heavy load.
Taller than when carrying a heavy load.
Shorter than when carrying a heavy load.
Less stable than when carrying a heavier load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taller than when carrying a heavy load.
questions.explanation: Heavy cargo weighs down a vehicle, making it sit lower. A lightly loaded vehicle sits higher. If your full vehicle fits under an overpass, an empty vehicle may not.

questions.question: When loading cargo, where should weight be placed?

options.text: As close to the cab as possible.

questions.explanation: Place cargo weight as low as possible to prevent the vehicle from tipping over.

questions.question: Is emergency equipment, such as a fire extinguisher, required?

options.text: Only for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT mean you have bad brakes?

options.text: Pads that are clean and dry

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads that are clean and dry
questions.explanation: Check your brakes for cracked drums, pads or shoes with oil or grease on them, and shoes that are worn too thin or broken.

questions.question: Driving with hanging meat in a trailer is challenging because:

options.text: It is not recommended during summer.
The load has a high center of gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: The load has a high center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is an unstable load. It has a high center of gravity, and the swinging meat can affect how you control the vehicle. Drive carefully with this type of cargo.

questions.question: A convex mirror is sometimes called a ____ mirror.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles use curved, convex mirrors. They are sometimes called fisheye, spot, or bug-eye mirrors. These mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Alcohol is removed from the body:

options.text: Faster if the person stays awake.

questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol from your body at a fixed rate. Drinking coffee or taking a cold shower will not speed this up. The only way to become sober is to wait for your body to remove the alcohol naturally.

questions.question: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Pull forward to the right, then back in a straight line.
Pull forward to the left, then back in a straight line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, first pull straight forward. Then back up to the right. Your vehicle must stay within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Explain what you would inspect and why.
Estimate the weight of a load in a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you would inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During the CDL vehicle inspection test, you must inspect your vehicle and explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.

questions.question: When starting a trip with cargo, the driver should:

options.text: Check the cargo within the first 50 miles of the trip.
Drive faster than usual to test the load security.
Only use the side mirrors to check the cargo.
Not check the cargo again if it was secured before starting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the cargo within the first 50 miles of the trip.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles after that.

questions.question: At speeds below 40 mph, maintain at least ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, allow one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use this same formula and add one more second. Large vehicles need more space to stop than small vehicles.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation:

options.text: The State will inform your employer.

questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic violation conviction in any vehicle. You must also report it to your licensing agency within 30 days if the violation happened in another state. Parking infractions are an exception to this rule.

questions.question: What color are ABS malfunction lamps?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow malfunction lamps.

questions.question: A bridge formula:

options.text: Allows less weight per axle when axles are close together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows less weight per axle when axles are close together.
questions.explanation: A bridge formula sets the maximum weight allowed on axles. Axles that are close together are allowed less weight than axles that are farther apart.

questions.question: If a vehicle comes with an inspection report, what should you do?

options.text: Inspect the vehicle first, then compare your notes with the report.
Read the report first when you do your inspection.
Skip your inspection and only use the report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the report first when you do your inspection.
questions.explanation: Before you inspect a vehicle, read any inspection report from the previous driver.

questions.question: What does a safety belt do?

options.text: Keeps you in place during a crash.
Allows you to move around inside the vehicle during a crash.
Makes it hard to drive the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps you in place during a crash.
questions.explanation: A safety belt holds you in your seat during a crash. This protects you from injury and helps you stay in control of the vehicle.

questions.question: How should cargo in a trailer be loaded?

options.text: It does not need to be secured.
It should be stacked no higher than three feet.
It should be secured so it doesn't move.
Heavy items should be placed on top of lighter items.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be secured so it doesn't move.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be secured to prevent it from shifting during travel. Load cargo to keep the vehicle balanced and stable.

questions.question: You need a CDL to drive a vehicle designed to carry how many people, including you?
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL to operate a vehicle designed to carry 16 or more people, including the driver.

questions.question: What happens when a driver is distracted?

options.text: They usually react well to hazards.
They usually notice things more slowly.
They usually know what's happening around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They usually notice things more slowly.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving slows your awareness and reaction time. Watch for distracted drivers and stay away from them when you can.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Assume the driver doesn't see you.
Wait for the other driver to signal that it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the driver doesn't see you.
questions.explanation: Always assume that other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians do not see you when you pass them.

questions.question: If you are convicted of driving with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.04 percent or higher, how long will you lose your CDL?
questions.explanation: A first conviction for driving with a BAC of 0.04 percent or higher means you will lose your CDL for at least one year.

questions.question: When driving at night, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Make sure your glasses are clean.

questions.explanation: Do not wear sunglasses when driving at night. Keep your eyeglasses clean and clear. Get enough rest before driving at night.

questions.question: When checking windshield wiper blades, they should be:
questions.explanation: Check wiper blades for damage, hardness, and that they are firmly attached.

questions.question: If you stop on the road or shoulder, what must you do within 10 minutes?

options.text: Stand behind your vehicle and wave traffic past.

questions.explanation: Within 10 minutes of stopping on the road, you must place emergency warning devices like reflective triangles.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT another name for convex mirrors?
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors have three other names: fisheye, spot, and bug-eye mirrors.

questions.question: Why are ice cream trucks hazardous to other drivers?

options.text: Ice cream trucks need to stay cold.
Children often run to ice cream trucks without looking for traffic.
Ice cream trucks leave water and ice on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Children often run to ice cream trucks without looking for traffic.
questions.explanation: Ice cream trucks are hazardous because they attract children. Children may run toward them without checking for other vehicles on the road.

questions.question: If you realize you may be running late, you should:

options.text: Drive with flashing lights so other drivers move out of your way.
Drive at a safe speed and arrive when you arrive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a safe speed and arrive when you arrive.
questions.explanation: To avoid dangerous driving, relax and accept delays. Plan for extra time when you schedule your trip to help reduce stress about arriving late.

questions.question: If you must drive in reverse, you should:

options.text: Drive as fast as possible to finish quickly.
First get out and walk around to check for obstacles.
Use only the passenger side mirror.
Stick your head out the window and look backward.

questions.correctAnswerText: First get out and walk around to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, walk around your vehicle to look for hazards in your path. Use both side mirrors while backing. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: When alley docking, you should first:

options.text: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Back up directly in front of the alley.
Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.
questions.explanation: To alley dock, first drive past the alley and stop parallel to its outer edge. Then back your vehicle straight into the parking space within the alley boundaries.

questions.question: When checking the exhaust system, which of these should be fixed?

options.text: Broken exhaust pipe, muffler, or tailpipe

questions.explanation: Exhaust system problems are serious because poisonous fumes can enter the cab. Check for loose or broken exhaust pipes, mufflers, tailpipes, brackets, and clamps. Also look for parts that are rubbing against fuel lines or tires, and parts that are leaking.

questions.question: When backing with a turning trailer, you should:

options.text: Do nothing. The trailer will naturally follow.
Change the direction of the steering wheel.
Turn the steering wheel harder in the direction it is already turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change the direction of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, first turn the steering wheel opposite to the direction you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts turning, reverse the steering wheel direction to follow it.

questions.question: Emergency brakes:
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must be held by mechanical force.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help avoid aggressive driving?

options.text: Not expecting any delays on your drive
Keeping your hands on the wheel
Not making gestures at other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Not expecting any delays on your drive
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, expect delays and plan travel time realistically. Also drive at a safe speed, keep a good following distance, avoid gesturing at other drivers, and keep both hands on the wheel.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, you should:
questions.explanation: With an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), brake the same way you would with any other braking system. Do not brake differently.

questions.question: How should you hold a steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand, keeping the other hand free for other tasks.
With one hand at a time, alternating between hands.
At the base of the wheel.

questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: If your brakes fail when driving downhill, why should you decide what to do quickly?

options.text: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
The longer you wait, the more vehicles will get out of your way.
The longer you wait, the slower your vehicle will go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
questions.explanation: Make your decision quickly if your brakes fail on a downhill slope. The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will be moving, and the harder it will be to stop.

questions.question: What is the name of thin ice that forms on road surfaces?
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. A road with black ice may look wet. Be very careful when temperatures are below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: What is a safety concern right when rain starts?

options.text: Water mixes with grease and oil on the road, making it slippery.
A driver may forget where the windshield wiper lever is.
People will use their windshield wipers unnecessarily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with grease and oil on the road, making it slippery.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first begins. Water mixes with oil and grease on the road that has not yet washed away.

questions.question: What is the minimum tire tread depth for front tires?
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth in every major groove. Other tires must have at least 2/32 of an inch of tread depth.

questions.question: How often should you do pre-trip inspections?

options.text: Differently each time, emphasizing different items.
The same way each time so you don't forget anything.
By someone other than the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time so you don't forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This helps you remember to check all important items.

questions.question: What danger could a cardboard box on the roadway pose?

options.text: It should be expected to be on the roadway.
It is usually empty and harmless.
It could contain a heavy object that damages vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It could contain a heavy object that damages vehicles.
questions.explanation: Any foreign object on the road can be dangerous. A cardboard box may look harmless, but it could contain something hard or heavy that damages your vehicle.

questions.question: What is the main cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.explanation: Speeding is the main cause of death and injury in work zones. Drive carefully near road workers.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead. This reduces sudden moves and gives the tailgater more room to pass. Do not speed up, as the tailgater may follow at the higher speed, which increases danger.

questions.question: What can happen when driving in extremely hot weather?

options.text: Requires you to remove oil from the engine.

questions.explanation: In extremely hot weather, tire pressure can increase to dangerous levels as air expands from heat. Keep enough oil and coolant in your engine to prevent overheating.
